claims.text: The category of ILogger<T> is the full name of T, so ILogger<RequestLoggingMiddleware> writes under DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging in .NET and ASP.NET Core, Log category

claims.text: Log levels in order: Trace, Debug, Information, Warning, Error, Critical (LogLevel enum; None disables).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging, Log level table; .NET API: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LogLevel

claims.text: Logging:LogLevel sets the minimum level per category; events below it are not written. A category uses the entry with the longest matching category-name prefix (Microsoft.AspNetCore covers Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics); otherwise Default applies.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging, Configure logging / How filtering rules are applied

claims.text: The console logger's formatter is chosen by Logging:Console:FormatterName; built-in names are simple, json and systemd; when not set, the simple formatter is used.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core / .NET docs: Console log formatting (Set formatter with configuration)

claims.text: The simple formatter prints an event as a header line (level: category[event id]) followed by an indented message line.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Console log formatting, Simple; devops.l2.why-monitoring (verified stage-1 output)

claims.text: The json formatter writes one JSON object per event on one line with EventId, LogLevel, Category, Message and State; State holds each template field by name plus {OriginalFormat} (the template, added by the logger).

docker-compose.yml@stage-2:128-132: the api service sets Logging__Console__FormatterName: "json"; the Logging section of appsettings.json and the log call in RequestLoggingMiddleware are unchanged from stage-1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang: git diff stage-1 stage-2 -- DonHang.Api/appsettings.json DonHang.Api/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs

claims.text: Environment variable Logging__Console__FormatterName sets configuration key Logging:Console:FormatterName (__ stands for :).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Configuration, Environment variables (__ separator)

claims.text: appsettings.json@stage-2 Logging:LogLevel: Default Information, Microsoft.AspNetCore Warning; so ASP.NET Core categories write only Warning and above while the API's own Information events are written.
Running the API with dotnet run outside Compose does not set Logging__Console__FormatterName, so the console uses the simple formatter (readable lines).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Api/appsettings.json (no Console:FormatterName), Properties/launchSettings.json if present; compose comment lines 130-131

claims.text: json-logs.sh (stage-2:10-24) sends GET /api/v1/products/2, reads docker compose logs --no-log-prefix --since 1m api, selects the line by Category and "Path" field, prints it raw and through jq from the lab box; output as outputs/stage-2/scripts/devops/json-logs.txt.
In the JSON line StatusCode and ElapsedMs are JSON numbers (200, not "200"), and Message holds the rendered sentence.
A minimum level of Warning still writes Warning, Error and Critical for that category and drops Trace, Debug, Information.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging, Log level ("logs at the specified level and higher")

claims.text: Filtering by level happens before the event is formatted/written; a filtered-out event is not written anywhere by the console provider.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging, How filtering rules are applied

claims.text: Try it: docker compose logs --no-log-prefix api | grep -c '"LogLevel":"Information","Category":"Microsoft.AspNetCore' prints 0; with "Warning" 0 or more; with DonHang instead of Microsoft.AspNetCore above 0 (live 2026-09-29: 0, 7, 59527).
claims.source_hint: live run on stage-2 lab 2026-09-29; Docker docs: docker compose logs (--no-log-prefix); grep -c

claims.text: Choosing the output format by configuration instead of code lets the same build print readable lines locally and JSON in the container.
